doc.title: George Russell — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Later years: recordings, Alice and the book
title: Volume II of the Concept
summary: Russell says Volume II will tie the Concept together and head toward physics and the stars.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Life philosophy: faith, karma and how to live

blocks.x: In the 21st-century, we’ve seen a completion of the book, again, The Lydian Chromatic Concept of Tonal Organization, volume I: The Art and Science of Tonal Gravity. That says to me that there’s a volume II in our future.
Sometimes I feel like a – I was going to say, almost said, sometimes I feel like a motherless child, because I used that song in the school program that was three . . .
I used – sometimes I used Sometimes I Feel Like a Motherless Child. It was very touching. But I lost what I should have been . . .
If I talk, I’m sure you’ll think of it, and then I want you to interrupt me.
I see that it says volume I: The Art and Science. Is there a volume II in our future?

Oh yes. There is a volume II. It’s the heart and soul – it puts all of this together and makes it possible to deal with it much easier and see the logic of it. As I said, there are hints that it’s getting into physics and the stars.
It is beautiful. You say in your epilogue in the book, which begins on page 235, “The major scale and the Lydian scale represent opposing forces in nature.”
